([[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]]) | college =[[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] (2012–2014) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | career_end = | highlights = *[[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] first team ([[2013–14 Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball season|2014]]) | medal_templates = }} '''Jordan Lavell Adams''' (born July 8, 1994){{cite news|title=Jordan Adams Bio|work=UCLABruins.com|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=207913793|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6NM0okQPt|archivedate=February 13, 2014|deadurl=no}} is a [[college basketball]] player for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. He was the first UCLA freshman to score 20 or more [[point (basketball)|points]] in his first four games, and an [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] first-team selection in the [[Pacific-12 Conference]] in his sophomore year. ==Early life== Adams was born in [[Atlanta]] to John Adams, a high school nutrition manager, and Sabrina Robinson Johnson, a dental hygienist. His parents never married but remained friends. When Adams was in the fourth grade and his life began to revolve around [[American football]] and [[basketball]], he moved from his mother's house to his father's. One of Adams' coaches was usually his father from when he was six until he was 16.{{cite news|last=Dave|first=Paresh|title=UCLA guard Jordan Adams' family goes the extra mile|date=December 6, 2013|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/college/ucla/la-sp-1207-ucla-jordan-adams-20131207,0,4073485,full.story|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6NLpRK38o|archivedate=February 13, 2014|deadurl=no}} Adams attended high school at [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] in [[Virginia]], where he was the ninth player in their basketball program's rich history to score 1,000 career points. He also played [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) basketball with the Atlanta Celtics. Shortly after Celtics' coach Korey McCray became an assistant coach at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), Adams accepted an [[athletic scholarship]] to play for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]].{{cite news|last=Holmes|first=Baxter|title=Unassuming Bruins guard Jordan Adams is first among equals|date=December 8, 2012|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://articles.latimes.com/2012/dec/08/sports/la-sp-1208-ucla-jordan-adams-20121208|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6NLljBGVZ|archivedate=February 13, 2014|deadurl=no}} ==College career== Adams in 2012 joined fellow incoming freshman [[Shabazz Muhammad]], [[Kyle Anderson (basketball)|Kyle Anderson]] and Tony Parker in a UCLA recruiting class considered the best in the nation. The first of the four recruits to sign, Adams was the only one that was not a [[McDonald's All-American]] in high school. Despite the competition, he remained committed to UCLA. He began the [[2012–13 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2012–13 season]] with 20 or more points in the first four games, becoming the first UCLA freshman to accomplish that feat; he was the first Bruin in any class to start the season with four straight since [[Don MacLean (basketball)|Don MacLean]] (6 straight) in [[1990–91 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|1990–91]].{{cite web|title=UCLA BASKETBALL – 2012-13 SEASON NOTES|publisher=UCLA Sports Information|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/fls/30500/pdf/MBKB_13SeasonNotes.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=30500|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6NMjDfB8i|archivedate=February 13, 2014|deadurl=no}} Though he did not start until the seventh game of the season, Adams was second on the team in scoring behind Muhammad. He finished the season starting in 27 of 33 games played, ranked eighth in the [[Pacific-12 Conference]] in scoring with 15.3 points per game, led the conference with 73 [[steal (basketball)|steals]], and was fourth with an 84.3 [[free throw percentage]].{{cite press release|title=No. 4-seed UCLA (26-8) vs. No. 13-seed Tulsa (21-12)|publisher=UCLA Sports Information|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/pdf9/2660851.pdf|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6ODsAqKw4|archivedate=March 20, 2014|deadurl=no}} UCLA coach [[Ben Howland]] and [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] coach [[Sean Miller]] were surprised that Adams did not make the conference's all-freshman team. Miller further believed that Adams should have been named to the [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12 team]] as well as the conference's all-defensive team.{{cite news|last=Yoon|first=Peter|title=Howland 'miffed' at Adams all-conference snub|date=March 12, 2013|work=ESPN.com|url=http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/UCLA/post/_/id/13556/howland-miffed-at-adams-all-conference-snub|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6NLpRKhFn|archivedate=February 13, 2014|deadurl=no}} In the semifinals of the [[2013 Pacific-12 Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2013 Pacific-12 Tournament]], Adams scored 11 points in the last six minutes in a comeback victory over Arizona. However be broke his right foot on the final play of the game; he had fractured the same foot in high school. Without Adams, the Bruins lost their next two games, including a season-ending loss to the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers]] in the opener of the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2013 NCAA Tournament]]. Two days after the season ended, Howland was fired and replaced by [[Steve Alford]]. Adams did not play basketball for four months while his foot healed. In his sophomore season in [[2013–14 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2013–14]], Adams said he enjoyed his role under Alford and his "very open" system, more so than he did with Howland.{{cite news|last=Carp|first=Steve|title=Adams, UCLA thrive in relaxed atmosphere|date=November 28, 2013|newspaper=Las Vegas
